decisions.reason: “Veteran of the banking trade” naturally preserves the financial-dealings context and voice.
The Korean 문득 supplies “suddenly,” which SOL drops.
“That happened” is a natural rendering of the same reference without changing the meaning.
“Helped themselves” preserves the colloquial accusation that they profited, while “had a hand in” preserves their involvement everywhere.
“The gap between rich and poor” naturally preserves the meaning of the income disparity.
The source says Ju would know the matter well, not specifically remember this item.
BASE preserves the established “Chief Escort” title; SOL replaces it with the unsupported “Escort Captain.”
“Separately” preserves the explicit sense of setting the item aside apart from the others.
SOL adds “delicate,” an unsupported characterization; the source contrasts a woman’s hand with a martial artist’s rough hand.
“Held it out” naturally renders the physical action of extending the slip, while the surrounding confusion remains clear.
“Multiplied like rabbits” naturally preserves the rapid-breeding image without unnecessary elaboration.
“Swindling” naturally captures the audacious 사기 행각 in this comic financial context.
“Went and doubled it” preserves the punchy poker-like escalation more naturally than “called it and doubled.”
“Half resigned himself to his fate” naturally conveys being halfway to giving up.
“His funeral rites” makes the clearly intended target explicit without changing the joke or action.
“Brought to light” naturally preserves the meaning of publicly revealing the facts.
“Before she had even turned twenty” is a natural and faithful rendering of being under the age of twenty.
“Lost so much to” and “her grief for those” preserve the causal and emotional relationships naturally.
“People I did not know” is natural English for the source’s reference to unfamiliar people.
The reordered sentence naturally states the total and preserves that all thirty-three died during this escort mission.
The trembling fist belongs to Hwangbo Eom, not Ju Hwaran; SOL changes the subject and is a factual error.
“That goes without saying” naturally conveys the emphatic Korean acceptance.
The glossary requires the protected relationship term “Senior Brother”; SOL uses an unsupported synonym.
“Fatal” preserves the source’s “치명적” severity; “disastrous” weakens the characterization of the mistake.
“Human losses” accurately preserves 인적 피해; “loss of life” narrows it specifically to deaths.
“Marveled at the sum” captures 혀를 내두르며 as astonishment, whereas “clicked her tongue” suggests disapproval.
The active phrasing naturally preserves that paying the sum would require removing half the sect’s foundations.
“Powerful voice” preserves the forceful quality of her voice; “firm” weakens it.
The source describes taking each person in with his eyes, not necessarily glaring at each one; SOL changes the action and attitude.
본산 means the sect’s main compound or headquarters, not simply the sect.
The source repeats “Murim” without an ellipsis; SOL changes the pause and delivery.
The recast naturally preserves the hollow laugh and the resulting cold expression.
“Retreating backs” naturally clarifies that they were leaving without changing the image.
The Korean explicitly includes “suddenly,” which SOL omits.
BASE preserves the definite sword and the direct contrast that he was not the one who drew it.
“Supple” preserves the source’s 낭창한 quality; “slender” adds a different physical trait and drops that texture.
